previousAssignment.assignment: Watch the complete named video, 0:00–5:18. Historical results describe the paper’s checkpoints and test conditions, not every later Whisper release.

replacementAssignment.label: Aleksa Gordić — Whisper paper walkthrough: architecture, tasks and data
replacementAssignment.assignment: Watch only 3:01–7:30 and 10:40–12:40 (6:29 total). Trace log-Mel input, encoder, cross-attending decoder, task/language/timestamp tokens and weakly supervised data filtering. Read paper §2 and Figure 1 for exact details. Skip the later code demonstration. These historical model details do not establish current release performance or authorise an inference run.

previousAssignment.label: NeurIPS 2020 / wav2vec 2.0 authors — self-supervised speech representations
previousAssignment.assignment: Watch the complete named video, 0:00–3:37. Trace the encoder, masking, contrastive targets and labelled adaptation in the authors’ wav2vec 2.0 explanation. Distinguish unlabelled pretraining from supervised fine-tuning. This original presentation does not establish multilingual performance or coverage; use the multilingual reading for that comparison.

replacementAssignment.label: Priyam Mazumdar — wav2vec 2.0 paper overview: pretraining and adaptation
replacementAssignment.assignment: Watch only 7:38–9:51, 31:15–32:31, 34:12–37:36 and 50:21–51:18 (7:50 total). Draw the convolutional features, masked Transformer context branch and separate unmasked quantized-target branch; distinguish contrastive pretraining from labelled CTC fine-tuning. Use paper §§2–3 for precise objectives and the separate multilingual reading for coverage claims. Skip implementation and the extended Gumbel/entropy derivations.

segments.label: Latent features, masking and quantized targets
Why mask spans of audio features
Contrastive targets and the diversity objective
